findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker interval for the entire cleanup service was changed from time.Minute * 10 to time.Minute * 1. This is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and greatly increases how often all cleanup jobs run, including snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, and query history. Since clean() has a 9-minute timeout and cleanup jobs can take a while, a 1-minute ticker can cause cleanup to run nearly continuously or back-to-back. If this was not intentional, it should be reverted or explicitly justified.

findings.title: Cleanup logs successful batch operations at error level
findings.body: The new batch cleanup code calls r.log.Error for every batch even when there is no error: see lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579. For example, after fetchIDs succeeds, line 534 logs 'Annotations to clean by time' with err=nil, and line 537 logs 'cleaned annotations by time' even when deleteByIDs returns nil. These calls happen for no-op batches with zero IDs and can include large 'ids' slices up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize (e.g. 32767). This floods logs with error-level events during normal cleanup, can trigger log-based alerts, and is misleading. Use Debug/Info for successful batch progress and avoid logging full ID slices at Error level.
